# runr_gateway_route (Resource)

A route of a gateway: a path that leads to a project's own workload, or to one of its [environments](https://runr.sh/docs/environments/#gateway-routes), with its authentication — public, an API key of a consumer, or a JWT ([API product](https://runr.sh/docs/api-product/#routes)). The gateway must be in the region the workload runs in (a global project: one of its regions), a path is used once per gateway, and a workload has one route. A route to the project's own workload makes the gateway its endpoint; removing the route gives it its own URL back. A key or JWT route is created with its authentication in one call: it is never public, not even for a moment.

Import with `<gateway id or region>/<route id or path>`: `terraform import runr_gateway_route.orders eu-1/orders`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# /orders leads to the orders project and asks for an API key (runr_api_key); the project's own
# URL stops serving, so callers cannot get around the keys.
resource "runr_gateway_route" "orders" {
  gateway_id   = runr_gateway.eu.id
  project_id   = runr_project.orders.id
  path         = "/orders"
  methods      = ["GET", "POST"]
  auth_mode    = "key"
  gateway_only = true
}

# /partners checks a JWT of the partners' identity provider; its sub claim names the consumer.
resource "runr_gateway_route" "partners" {
  gateway_id = runr_gateway.eu.id
  project_id = runr_project.partners.id
  path       = "/partners"
  auth_mode  = "jwt"
  jwt = {
    jwks_url         = "https://id.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json"
    issuer           = "https://id.example.com/"
    audience         = "partners-api"
    require_consumer = true
  }
}

# The staging environment of the orders project, on its own path.
resource "runr_gateway_route" "orders_staging" {
  gateway_id  = runr_gateway.eu.id
  project_id  = runr_project.orders.id
  environment = "staging"
  path        = "/orders-staging"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `gateway_id` (String) Gateway id (`runr_gateway`). Changing it creates a new route.
- `path` (String) Path of the route, e.g. `/orders`. Changes in place (the route keeps its id, which API key scopes name).
- `project_id` (String) Project id. Changing it creates a new route.

### Optional

- `auth_mode` (String) `public` (anyone, default), `key` (an API key of a consumer of the gateway or the organization: `runr_api_key`) or `jwt` (a JWT the route's JWKS verifies; set `jwt`). Key and JWT routes are checked by the region's gateway-auth and answer 503 `auth_unavailable` until it is ready (the gateway's `status`).
- `environment` (String) Name or id of the project environment the route leads to. Left out (or `production`): the project's own workload. Changing it creates a new route.
- `gateway_only` (Boolean) Only through the gateway: the workload's own URL stops serving, so callers cannot get around the route's keys. Refused for a workload with custom domains and for a global project. Left out: kept as it is (a new route: `false`).
- `jwt` (Attributes) How a `jwt` route verifies tokens (required with `auth_mode = "jwt"`, refused otherwise). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--jwt))
- `methods` (Set of String) Methods the route accepts (`GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`). Left out: every method.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Route id.
- `url` (String) URL of the route (on the gateway's custom domain once it is verified).

<a id="nestedatt--jwt"></a>
### Nested Schema for `jwt`

Required:

- `jwks_url` (String) JWKS of the token issuer (fetched from inside the region).

Optional:

- `audience` (String) Expected `aud` claim.
- `issuer` (String) Expected `iss` claim.
- `require_consumer` (Boolean) `true`: a valid token whose subject is no consumer gets 403. `false` (default): it passes without a plan and its usage is counted under the subject.
- `subject_claim` (String) Claim that names the consumer (its `jwt_subject`; default `sub`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <gateway id or region>/<route id or path>
terraform import runr_gateway_route.orders eu-1/orders
```
